label: rem:local-q-zeta-function-remark
title: Frobenius eigenvalues of Bring's curve
html: The geometric Riemann hypothesis constrains the absolute values of the Frobenius eigenvalues of Bring's curve; the local q-zeta function packages those eigenvalues as a single generating function. Because g = 4 for Bring's curve, the polynomial P(t) has degree 2g = 8. The roots \alpha_1, \ldots, \alpha_8 are the fundamental eigenvalues of the Frobenius action on the first étale cohomology. The denominator factors (1-t) and (1-qt) correspond to H^0 and H^2 respectively.
